n: Section 20, the “Articles and Covenants,” served as the Church’s founding constitution. It opens by dating the Church’s organization: April 6, 1830, legally established under the laws of the United States and by God’s command.

f.w: agreeable to the laws of our country
f.g: The Church was organized under New York law at the Peter Whitmer Sr. home in Fayette.

f.w: the sixth day of the month which is called April

n: Joseph Smith was called and ordained an apostle and the first elder of the Church.

f.w: ordained an apostle of Jesus Christ

n: Oliver Cowdery was called as an apostle and second elder, ordained by Joseph. On April 6 they ordained each other elders after the members sustained them.

f.w: the second elder of this church

n: All this came by Christ’s grace, to whom all glory belongs.
A brief history: after Joseph was told his sins were forgiven (in the First Vision), he became “entangled again in the vanities of the world” — youthful mistakes he later openly admitted.

f.w: received a remission of his sins
entangled again in the vanities of the world

n: After Joseph sincerely repented, an angel — Moroni — appeared, with a face like lightning and robes whiter than anything on earth.
The angel gave Joseph inspiring commandments.
God gave Joseph power to translate the Book of Mormon through means prepared beforehand — the Urim and Thummim.

f.w: the means which were before prepared

n: The Book of Mormon tells of a fallen people and contains the fulness of Christ’s gospel for Gentiles and Jews.
It was given by inspiration and confirmed to the witnesses by angels.

f.w: confirmed to others by the ministering of angels

n: The Book of Mormon proves the Bible is true and that God still calls prophets today, just as anciently.

f.w: Proving to the world that the holy scriptures are true

n: This shows that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

f.w: the same God yesterday, today, and forever

n: With such strong witnesses, the world will be judged by how it responds to this work.
Those who accept it in faith and live righteously receive a crown of eternal life.
Those who reject it in unbelief bring condemnation on themselves.
The elders testify that they have heard these words from God, the “glorious Majesty on high.”
Here begins a summary of core doctrine. From these witnesses we know there is an infinite, eternal, unchanging God, Creator of heaven and earth.
God created man, male and female, in his own image and likeness.

f.w: after his own image and in his own likeness

n: He commanded them to love, serve, and worship him alone, the only true and living God.
Through transgression, humanity became fallen — “sensual and devilish,” subject to worldly appetites.
So God gave his Only Begotten Son, as the scriptures testify.
Christ was tempted but did not give in.

f.w: He suffered temptations but gave no heed unto them

n: He was crucified, died, and rose again on the third day.
He ascended to heaven to sit at the Father’s right hand and reign with power.

f.w: on the right hand of the Father

n: All who believe, are baptized in his name, and endure in faith will be saved.
This includes not only those after Christ’s earthly ministry (“the meridian of time”) but also all believers before him who accepted the prophets’ testimony of him.

f.g: the middle or high point of history, when Christ lived on earth.

f.w: who truly testified of him in all things

n: It also includes those afterward who believe in the gifts of God through the Holy Ghost, who testifies of the Father and the Son.
The Father, Son, and Holy Ghost are “one God” — united perfectly in purpose. Latter-day Saints understand them as three distinct beings.
All must repent, believe in Jesus Christ, worship the Father in his name, and endure to the end to be saved.
Justification — being declared innocent and pardoned — comes through Christ’s grace and is just and true.

f.g: being pardoned and declared right with God.

n: Sanctification — being made holy — also comes through Christ’s grace, to those who love and serve God with all their heart, might, mind, and strength.

f.g: the process of being made pure and holy.

n: But it’s possible to fall from grace and depart from God. Salvation requires continued faithfulness.
So the Church must be careful and pray always to avoid temptation.

f.w: pray always, lest they fall into temptation

n: Even the sanctified must stay watchful.
These teachings agree with John’s Revelation, adding nothing to it or taking anything away, nor to future revelations from God.

f.w: neither adding to, nor diminishing from the prophecy of his book

n: God has spoken; honor and glory to his name.

Requirements for baptism: humility, desire, a broken heart and contrite spirit, true repentance, willingness to take Christ’s name and serve him to the end, and works showing the Spirit’s influence. These remain the basic qualifications today.

f.w: willing to take upon them the name of Jesus Christ

n: Now the duties of priesthood holders and members are outlined. An apostle is also an elder and is called to baptize.
Elders may ordain other elders, priests, teachers, and deacons.

f.g: Greek diakonos, “servant”; an office of the Aaronic Priesthood.

n: They administer the sacrament — the bread and wine as emblems of Christ’s flesh and blood.

f.w: the emblems of the flesh and blood of Christ

n: They confirm baptized members by the laying on of hands for the gift of the Holy Ghost.

f.w: the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost

n: Elders teach, explain, encourage, baptize, and watch over the Church.
They confirm members by laying on hands and bestowing the Holy Ghost.
Elders lead all meetings.
Elders conduct meetings as the Holy Ghost directs.

f.w: as they are led by the Holy Ghost

n: A priest’s duties: preach, teach, explain, encourage, baptize, and administer the sacrament.
Priests also visit members’ homes, encouraging vocal and private prayer and faithfulness to family duties.

f.w: visit the house of each member
f.g: an early form of what later became home teaching and ministering.

n: Priests may ordain other priests, teachers, and deacons.
A priest leads meetings when no elder is present.
When an elder is present, the priest focuses on preaching, teaching, and baptizing.
He continues visiting homes and encouraging prayer and family duties.
Priests assist the elders whenever needed.
A teacher’s duty is to watch over the Church always, being with and strengthening members.
Teachers help ensure there is no sin, hard feelings, lying, backbiting, or gossip among members — caring for the Church’s spiritual health.

f.g: speaking badly of someone behind their back.

n: They encourage members to meet often and to do their duty.
Teachers lead meetings when no elder or priest is present.
Deacons assist teachers in their duties when needed.
Teachers and deacons cannot baptize, administer the sacrament, or lay on hands.
Yet they can warn, explain, encourage, teach, and invite everyone to come to Christ — a calling open to every priesthood holder.

f.w: invite all to come unto Christ

n: Every priesthood holder must be ordained according to God’s call and gifts, by the power of the Holy Ghost in the one who ordains.

f.w: according to the gifts and callings of God unto him

n: Elders are to meet in conference every three months, or as directed. The first conference met in June 1830.

f.g: a gathering of Church leaders and members for instruction and business.

n: These conferences handle whatever Church business is necessary.
Elders receive licenses — written certificates of authority — from other elders by vote of their congregation or conference.

f.g: written certificates showing one’s ordination and authority.

n: Priests, teachers, and deacons ordained by a priest may receive a certificate to present for a license.
No one is ordained in an organized branch without the vote of its members — the principle of common consent.

f.w: without the vote of that church
f.g: the principle of “common consent,” in which members sustain those called.

n: Where no branch exists, certain leaders may ordain without a vote. (This verse names offices added in later editions as the Church grew.)

f.w: traveling bishops, high councilors, high priests
f.g: these offices were not yet organized in 1830; this wording reflects later updates to the revelation.

n: Presiding high priests, bishops, high councilors, and high priests are ordained under direction of a high council or general conference.
New members should be taught enough about the Church before partaking of the sacrament and being confirmed, so all is done in order.

f.w: so that all things may be done in order

n: Members should show by godly conduct and speech that they are worthy, with works and faith that match scripture.

f.g: “conversation” in older English means one’s whole conduct or way of life.

n: Members are to bring their children before the Church for elders to bless them in Christ’s name — the origin of the baby blessing.

f.w: lay their hands upon them in the name of Jesus Christ, and bless them

n: Only those who have reached accountability and can repent may join the Church.
Here is how baptism is performed for those who repent.
Someone with authority from Christ goes into the water with the candidate, calls them by name, and speaks this prayer — the same words used today.

f.w: Having been commissioned of Jesus Christ

n: Then the person is fully immersed and brought up again — symbolizing burial and new life with Christ.
The Church should meet often to partake of the sacrament in remembrance of Jesus.
An elder or priest kneels with the congregation and offers this solemn prayer.
The sacrament prayer on the bread, nearly identical to Moroni 4:3 — evidence that the restored Church followed the Book of Mormon pattern.
Instructions for blessing the cup.
The sacrament prayer on the wine, matching Moroni 5:2. Today water is used, as later permitted in D&C 27.
Members who sin are to be handled as scripture directs — with a balance of justice and mercy.
Each congregation should send teachers to the elders’ conferences.
They should bring lists of new members, so that one appointed elder can keep a complete record of all Church members.

f.w: a regular list of all the names of the whole church

n: Names of those excommunicated are removed from the general Church record.
Members moving to a new congregation may carry a letter certifying their good standing — an early form of the membership record transfer.
